### PAT-approval-that-returns

### PAT-compensation-for-the-irreversible

- cancel_order is irreversible, and the step after it can still fail
- issue_refund is irreversible, and the step after it can still fail

### PAT-delivery-id-at-the-edge

- cancel_order.identity declares what makes a repeat a repeat

- issue_refund.identity declares what makes a repeat a repeat

### PAT-escalation-with-lapse

- P-ESC-TTL: a queued escalation nobody comes to lapses

### PAT-exchange-safe-reduction

- Q-TOOL-RESULT: a tool result enters context at most 8000 characters long

### PAT-fenced-provenance

- order.note is untrusted — content, never instruction

### PAT-port-with-a-null-object

- cancel_order.on_refusal: what is offered when it cannot be done
- change_address.on_refusal: what is offered when it cannot be done
- escalate.on_refusal: what is offered when it cannot be done

### PAT-registry-of-declared-handlers

- P-DIRECT names the answerable intents

### PAT-router-ahead-of-loop

- P-DIRECT: order status and refund status are answered from the order system deterministically, with no model call, when the turn names one intent and carries an order id; anything ambiguous or multi-intent goes to the loop

### PAT-versioned-rule-set

- escalation rules are a list, and first match wins
- the refusal list is normative and changes
